title: AND-normalization at most doubles circuit size
statement: Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ variables, where the size of a circuit is its total number of nodes, counting internal AND/OR gates together with literal leaves. Normalizing $c$ into strictly alternating AND-normal form — a literal becoming a singleton clause, an AND gate normalizing each child into OR-normal form, and an OR gate becoming a single wrapping OR node over its children's AND-normal forms — yields a normal-form AND circuit whose size is at most twice the size of $c$.
hypotheses_covered: c is a Boolean circuit on n variables
